why: The statement asks to determine the growth rate of r_k(N); no event supplies matching upper and lower bounds for any k, so every substantive event is a bound (F4), including the post-snapshot ones: Hunter and EHPS (k=3 Behrend constant), LSS (k>=5 upper bound), Raghavan (k=3 exponent 1/6) and the OpenAI claim (stretched-exponential upper bound for all k>=3). I did not score per-k bounds as 'case', since even for a single k nothing is determined. Hunter's v1 of 29 Jan 2024 is three days after the snapshot. EPS (finite groups), corners, primes and the finite-field ergodic constant are variants; the LSS inverse theorem is a tool with no bound of its own (none). Kalai's digest of EHPS describes the result without a check, so EHPS stays unreviewed. The two OpenAI rows describe one release, judged identically: AI-generated per the README's repository-wide statement (family 159 is not among the named exceptions), doubtful but not set aside.
doubts: The two OpenAI events duplicate one release. Its AI attribution rests on a repository-wide README sentence, not a family-level statement. The second OpenAI entry says k=3's exponent is not improved, so for k=3 it is no bound advance; the claim moves k>=4. Raghavan's setting ({1..N} vs Z/NZ) is unresolved but immaterial to the scope.
